title: Structure-Guided Texture Enhancement and Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for Progressive Mural Inpainting
abstract: Progressive mural inpainting requires structural guidance to reconstruct missing textures while maintaining color consistency. Existing methods only introduce line constraints at the input stage, resulting in distorted structures and color mismatch for severely damaged murals. This paper proposes SGMA-MuralNet, a two-stage network integrating structure-conditioned deep feature modulation and multi-scale feature aggregation (MFA). A full-line encoder applies affine modulation on channel-local normalized features in middle encoder layers to retain fine mural structures. The MFA module uses parallel dilated convolutions and channel recalibration to capture multi-range context. A color correction network (CCN) predicts signed residual for color alignment, and mask compositing keeps intact original pixels. Evaluated on DhMurals1714 with 10&ndash;60% irregular damage masks, our model reaches 28.65 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), 0.926 structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and 0.034 learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS), outperforming MuralNet with +1.37 dB PSNR and 30.6% LPIPS reduction. Visual results verify its capability to restore facial contours and flowing ribbons with coherent color transitions. The contribution is an incremental architectural integration of established structural conditioning and multi-scale aggregation mechanisms within MuralNet&rsquo;s progressive structure reconstruction network (SRN)&ndash;CCN framework. The reported results support its utility for benchmark mural inpainting conditioned on supplied registered drawings; they do not establish the historical authenticity of generated details.

title: Semantic Federated Clustering for Cross-Domain Recommendation with Interaction Graphs
abstract: In federated cross-domain recommendation, the existing research has widely focused on scenarios where at least some users or items overlap. How to enable cross-domain recommendation over non-overlapping users and items has emerged as a challenging research direction. However, current privacy-preserving cross-domain recommendation methods struggle to achieve effective semantic alignment across domains in such scenarios, hindering their ability to capture latent correlations between interaction graphs. Moreover, when refining noisy node representations and interaction sequences, these methods often overlook temporal noise implicitly embedded in semantic information, as well as the potential of jointly leveraging textual and temporal features for collaborative denoising. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Semantic Federated Clustering-driven Cross-Domain Recommendation model (SFC-CDR). Specifically, we first design a clustering-anchored contrastive learning framework that performs clustering using weighted multi-layer node semantic representations. The weighted aggregated centroids serve as semantic anchors to dynamically update the pool of positive and negative samples in contrastive learning, thereby achieving geometric alignment in the shallow feature space and capturing fine-grained semantic correlations in the implicit concept space. Furthermore, we design a Joint Temporal&ndash;Frequency Filtering (JTFF) module. In the frequency domain, features are processed via an MoE adapter and FFT-based filtering, while in the temporal domain, a temporal convolutional network (TCN) is employed to model temporal patterns in user&ndash;item interaction sequences. The resulting temporal and frequency-domain representations are integrated through Temporal&ndash;Frequency Refinement Gating (TFRG), enabling complementary refinement of node semantic representations and user behavior sequences. Extensive experiments conducted on four real-world datasets demonstrate that SFC-CDR outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Disciplinary Cultures and the Diffusion of Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Bibliometric Study of Music and Acoustics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in scientific research and artistic practice, yet its publication patterns vary across research contexts. This study presents a comparative bibliometric analysis of 655 publications retrieved from five databases. We examine publication trends, authorship patterns, national contributions, application areas, and the reported use of AI model families across three analytical categories: STEM&ndash;Sound-only (SSO), STEM&ndash;Music-explicit (SME), and Music-Focused AI (MFAI), where STEM denotes science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. The corpus comprises 139 SSO, 496 SME, and 20 MFAI publications. Publication output increased markedly after 2018, particularly in SSO and SME. Within the retrieved corpus, recurrent neural networks, convolutional neural networks, and Transformers appeared earlier in SME than in SSO, whereas MFAI included earlier work applying machine learning to sound design. Sole-authored papers accounted for 60% of MFAI publications, compared with 15.5% in SME and 2.2% in SSO. China had the largest publication count in SSO and SME, while no contributions from Chinese institutional affiliations were identified in the MFAI sample. These findings document differences in research output, collaboration patterns, geographical participation, and the timing of reported model use across publication contexts. They provide an empirical basis for further investigation of interdisciplinary exchange.

title: Greedy and Stepwise Feature Selection for Network Intrusion Detection: A Systematic Review and Decision Workflow
abstract: Feature selection is widely used in machine-learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs/NIDSs) to reduce dimensionality and computational burden, yet its benefits are difficult to attribute when feature evaluation, subset search, preprocessing, classifier design, and deployment conditions are assessed together. This systematic review analyzed 104 IDS/NIDS studies published from 2010 to 2026, identified through Scopus and Web of Science and supplemented by targeted Google Scholar searches. The corpus comprised 56 filter/relevance, 18 greedy/sequential, 28 hybrid/metaheuristic contrast, and 2 Other/Unclear studies. We assessed feature reduction, computational reporting, repeated-run evidence, feature-subset stability, leakage control, online cost, and deployment evidence. Among 42 studies with a single unambiguous reduction value, the median feature reduction was 73.8% (IQR: 59.3&ndash;84.2%). The runtime or computational cost was reported in 56.7% of studies and independent repeated runs in 9.6%, and no study explicitly evaluated feature-subset stability. Leakage-safe processing was clearly demonstrated in 13.5%, whereas 56.7% presented potential leakage risk; clear or partial deployment evidence was available in 6.7%. Out of six strict same-study comparisons, broader hybrid/metaheuristic methods improved reported detection performance in five, but gains in feature reduction and computational cost were inconsistent. Based on these findings, the review formulates feature-selection choice as a resource-constrained decision problem and proposes an algorithmic conditional-escalation workflow in which a broader search is introduced only when simpler strategies fail to satisfy predefined predictive or operational constraints. Additional search complexity should therefore be justified by comparable, reproducible, leakage-safe, and deployment-relevant evidence rather than by cross-study accuracy alone.

title: Multi-Level Transformations Induced by GenAI in Instructional Design: A Thematic Analysis of a Reddit Forum
abstract: Research on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) integration into instructional design practice has been expanding rapidly; however, its effects on the instructional design profession remain underexplored. To this end, this study examines instructional designers&rsquo; perceptions about how GenAI is reshaping the instructional design professional landscape and how online communities engage them in sharing those perceptions. Using a mixed-methods data analysis method including automatic text mining and human verification, a large data set obtained from an online community of instructional designers on Reddit was analyzed thematically. Results revealed three key changes at professional, organizational, and individual levels, and the mechanisms shaping instructional designers&rsquo; engagement in their online community. Namely, GenAI has already started to reshape the instructional design landscape through a mixed set of changes including transformations, adaptations and reconfigurations, and an online community can function as an informal community of practice for instructional designers to collectively share experiential wisdom and necessary competencies to successfully navigate the emergent transitions. This study contributes by uncovering the changes happening in instructional design due to GenAI and how informal online channels can work as communities of practice that are distributed, asynchronous, on-demand knowledge exchange avenues, thus increasing instructional designers&rsquo; awareness and collective preparedness.

title: A Leakage-Aware Evaluation Framework and Benchmark for Edge-Based Multi-Sensor Fire and Smoke Detection
abstract: Low-cost multi-sensor nodes are increasingly used to detect fire and smoke inside buildings, where separating flame from smouldering emission determines the response. Such detectors are usually validated on densely sampled logs whose consecutive readings are nearly identical. Earlier studies report near-perfect accuracy in this setting but seldom state whether the train&ndash;test split respected event boundaries; when it does not, the score measures memorisation rather than generalisation. This paper treats the evaluation itself as the object of study. A controlled single-room testbed with temperature, humidity, gas, and particulate sensing produced a labelled time-series dataset with exactly known event boundaries, so that leakage could be introduced or excluded deliberately. Six methods were evaluated on identical data under a random split and under an event-preserving split using the macro-averaged F1 score, which weights minority classes equally. The random split yielded markedly higher three-class scores for every supervised model, whereas hazard-versus-normal detection was largely unaffected. Holding out single events revealed strong between-event variability, while thinning records within events changed results only slightly: independent events, not records, are the binding constraint. The dataset, code, and a short leakage-aware protocol are released; the findings characterise the evaluation protocol under controlled conditions, not field performance.

title: An Integrated ETL&ndash;OLAP and Semantic Retrieval Architecture for Hybrid Analysis of Structured and Unstructured Enterprise Data
abstract: Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) and Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) provide robust mechanisms for integrating structured data and supporting multidimensional analysis. Still, they offer limited support for semantic access to unstructured textual content. This study proposes an integrated architecture that combines conventional ETL and data warehousing with semantic retrieval based on dense vector representations and similarity search. The architecture separates structured analytical processing from semantic document retrieval while preserving traceability among source documents, warehouse records, and vector representations. The architecture was examined through an implementation-oriented case study using a large document collection of up to 1.58 million PDF files. The study reports descriptive implementation observations on data ingestion, vector indexing, and query execution in the deployed environment. These observations characterize the operational behavior of the implemented system and are not presented as a controlled performance benchmark between OLAP and semantic retrieval, because the two mechanisms address different classes of information needs. The architecture also provides a query-time foundation for downstream Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG); however, this study does not assess generative response quality or LLM orchestration as case-study outcomes. Accordingly, this work contributes primarily through the architectural integration of structured analytical processing and semantic retrieval, preservation of document-to-warehouse-to-vector traceability, and practical implementation of the framework over a large enterprise document repository. The study also identifies limitations related to repeated timing measurements, stage-level profiling, independently annotated relevance judgments, and retrieval-effectiveness assessment. These limitations define future work involving Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG, controlled workload benchmarking, and systematic evaluation of RAG-generated responses.

title: DyGRAV: Dynamic Grounding and Relational Reasoning for Vision&ndash;Language Navigation
abstract: Vision&ndash;Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to interpret natural-language instructions in 3D environments. While significant progress has been made, state-of-the-art agents often struggle with instructions that demand fine-grained visual understanding, correctly grounding specific object attributes, distinguishing between similar objects, and interpreting complex spatial relationships. Many methods rely on static visual features or on global cross-modal attention and lack mechanisms to dynamically resolve ambiguities during navigation. We propose DyGRAV (Dynamic Grounding and Relational Reasoning for VLN), which is a dynamic, uncertainty-aware framework that augments a strong VLN backbone with two adaptively triggered reasoning modules. The Contextual VLM Querying module detects grounding ambiguity for descriptive phrases (e.g., &ldquo;the ceramic bowl&rdquo;) and issues targeted queries to a vision&ndash;language model (e.g., CLIP) using current visual evidence, while the Incremental Relational Scene Graph (IRSG) constructs lightweight, task-relevant relational memory online to resolve complex spatial relations (e.g., &ldquo;the chair next to the window&rdquo;). A budget-aware gating mechanism regulates when these modules are invoked, optimizing the balance between reasoning quality and computational cost through value-per-cost selection and hard budget constraints. Comprehensive evaluations on R2R and RxR, along with a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark emphasizing attribute and relation understanding, show that DyGRAV achieves superior navigation accuracy on challenging instructions while maintaining bounded per-step compute budgets with 97.33% episode-level adherence.

title: LAB@SMART: A Digital Workflow for Continuous Formative Assessment in FPGA-Based Digital Systems Laboratories
abstract: The digital transformation of engineering education has created new opportunities to support laboratory learning through continuous formative assessment. However, digital technologies are frequently implemented as isolated tools rather than as components of a coherent pedagogical framework. This paper presents LAB@SMART, an integrated digital framework that supports the complete FPGA-based laboratory learning cycle by combining pre-laboratory preparation, in-class formative assessment, laboratory practice, post-laboratory consolidation, and continuous feedback within a unified workflow. The framework integrates complementary digital technologies with conventional laboratory teaching without requiring modifications to the curriculum or laboratory infrastructure. A pilot deployment was conducted during the second semester of the 2025/2026 academic year in a Digital Systems Laboratory course involving two laboratory groups (35 students). The evaluation combined academic performance, informal implementation observations, and an anonymous student questionnaire. Among students who attended the examinations, the pilot groups showed a slightly higher pass rate than the remaining course cohort while also obtaining a slightly higher average final grade. Students also reported positive perceptions of the integrated workflow, particularly regarding laboratory preparation, continuous monitoring of their learning progress, and formative feedback. Although the pilot was limited in duration and scale, the results provide preliminary evidence of the practical feasibility of the proposed framework and support its further evaluation in other engineering laboratory contexts.

title: The Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Self-Regulated Learning: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: This meta-analysis systematically examined the effects of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on students&rsquo; self-regulated learning (SRL), including its overall effectiveness and its impact on the cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioral dimensions of SRL. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this study conducted a random-effects meta-analysis to synthesize evidence from 17 studies. The results revealed a statistically significant positive average effect of GenAI on SRL (Hedges&rsquo; g = 0.74). Nevertheless, substantial between-study heterogeneity suggested considerable variation in the magnitude of this effect across educational contexts. Positive average effects were also observed across the cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, and behavioral dimensions of SRL. However, a multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with CR2-robust inference indicated that effect sizes did not differ significantly across these dimensions (p = 0.564). Moderator analyses revealed significant differences in effect sizes associated with experimental design and intervention duration, whereas no significant differences were observed for subject domain, GenAI intervention type, GenAI tool, or personalization. Overall, the findings suggest that GenAI has the potential to contribute to the development of SRL, highlighting the importance of using GenAI as a scaffold to support, rather than replace, learners&rsquo; active self-regulatory processes.

title: Event Log Behavioral Privacy Protection Method Based on Relaxed Behavioral Profiles
abstract: Privacy preservation techniques for event logs prevent sensitive information leakage by injecting noise into log data, thus mitigating privacy risks in business process management. While ensuring privacy, this approach often reduces data utility and impacts subsequent analysis accuracy. Current research mainly optimizes noise injection based on data attributes to preserve utility, but overlooks how behavioral relationship changes affect data quality. To address this, this paper proposes a privacy protection method for event logs based on relaxed behavioral profiles. First, a behavioral privacy attack model is formalized to reveal how behavioral relationships can lead to privacy leakage. Building on this, data attributes are utilized to extend behavioral profiles, and a behavioral profile extension algorithm is proposed to analyze implicit behavioral relationships between activities. This allows building a multi-perspective perturbation set combining behavioral and data attributes. Finally, perturbations are injected using differential privacy methods. Experiments on both real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that the event logs generated by this method are behavior-unchanged at the level of the modeled relations, effectively mitigating the utility loss caused by log anonymization and attaining F1-scores of up to 0.874 on synthetic data, comparable to those of the baselines.

title: Shipping in 76 Locales: A Multi-Case Study of LLM-Agent Localization Pipelines for Production Mobile Apps
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents translate software interfaces at scale, yet production evidence on what breaks&mdash;and which safeguards catch it&mdash;is nearly absent: a 2026 mapping study of localization testing retained 24 primary studies, though none on LLM-driven localization. We report a multi-case study of fourteen shipped mobile apps by one developer (ten iOS, four Android; 40&ndash;76 locales; roughly 347,000 units) at five maturity levels. Mining the repositories (catalogs, 4473 commits, process documents, tooling), we code defects into thirteen classes in two waves, the second under a frozen codebook, and map each to its detecting layer. Translation quality is not independently measured; the defect record is a lower bound. Of 468 commit-anchored defects, process and coverage gaps&mdash;strings escaping the pipeline&mdash;are modal in each wave (26.7% and 27.5%); placeholder errors are near-absent (9 in 347,000 units). LLM judges are the largest operational detector (26.7%), ahead of humans (16.0%) and validators (13.7%), yet 127 defects (27.1%) escaped every layer until our audit. What escapes tracks validator scope, not maturity alone. Layered validation, not prompt-level care, determines what reaches users. Translation takes minutes; the validation stack is the lasting cost. We derive six testable propositions and ten guidelines, and release the codebook, dataset, and scripts.

title: SparseRoute: Structured Sparse Variable Routing for High-Dimensional Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Forecasting high-dimensional multivariate time series requires models to represent dependencies across variables without making variable interactions prohibitively expensive. Full attention over variable-level tokens has a pairwise cost quadratic in the number of variables; channel-independent methods avoid this cost but omit explicit cross-variable interactions. SparseRoute addresses this design choice by assigning variables to a small set of learned subspaces and applying attention to their aggregated representations. A vector-quantization routing module produces hard variable-to-subspace assignments, while a straight-through estimator supplies surrogate gradients during training. A dual-path decoder combines subspace predictions broadcast to their assigned variables with variable-level predictions from a shared multilayer perceptron. We evaluate the model with three seeds on Traffic, Electricity, Solar-Energy, PEMS04, and PEMS07. SparseRoute obtains the lowest mean MAE for Traffic at horizon 96 and the lowest mean MSE at horizon 192; Crossformer leads on several other dataset&ndash;horizon pairs. Relative to a dense variable-token model with matched tokenization and backbone, routing changes the pairwise attention factor from the square of the variable count to the square of the subspace count; this theoretical comparison does not establish an end-to-end resource advantage over the external baselines.

title: A Mobile-Centric Approach to Improving the Performance of Decentralized Wireless Networks
abstract: The proliferation of wireless devices and intelligent environments has led to increasingly dense, interference-prone Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) deployments. Recent amendments, such as IEEE 802.11ax/be, aim to enhance spatial reuse (SR) by optimizing spectrum efficiency. However, current SR initiatives face significant deployment challenges, including incompatibility with legacy 802.11 versions, a lack of centralized coordination, the difficulty for Access Points (APs) to monitor their neighborhood while maintaining uninterrupted service, and limited monitoring range. We argue that these limitations stem from the traditional AP-centric approach. In contrast, this work proposes a mobile-centric SR approach that overcomes these issues. Our method uses roaming mobile terminals (MTs) to independently monitor neighboring AP parameters (channel, transmission power, carrier-sense threshold), regardless of the 802.11 version or owner. After collecting local topological information, MTs execute a two-stage optimization: first, a local channel selection heuristic, followed by an algorithm that uses a pre-trained neural network to quickly evaluate and select the best transmission power and carrier-sense threshold for each in-range AP. MTs then broadcast these recommended parameters opportunistically using unassociated management frames, allowing them to be modified on the fly. By using a pre-trained model, our system does not need to learn in real time; consequently, network convergence is primarily governed by how quickly the mobile terminals explore and cover the deployment area, which depends on factors such as terminal speed, number of mobile terminals, trajectory characteristics, and pause times. Simulation results demonstrate that this mobile-centric approach quickly identifies near-optimal AP configurations, achieving throughput performance comparable to the reinforcement learning approaches considered in this study while exhibiting substantially shorter estimate

title: A Conversational AI Framework for Teacher Training
abstract: This paper introduces ETQ-AI (Effective Teaching Questionnaire&mdash;Artificial Intelligence), a conversational AI framework designed to support teacher professional development by identifying pedagogical misconceptions and fostering critical reflection. Building on Evidence-Informed Education (EIE) principles, the system integrates a 50-item diagnostic questionnaire with an automated, Gemini-driven Explainable AI (XAI) feedback layer. When teachers complete the diagnostic form, they receive personalized feedback and can engage in dialogic interactions with Google Gemini to explore the underlying meta-analytic evidence (e.g., Hattie&rsquo;s effect sizes, Cognitive Load Theory) or argue personal objections. We evaluated system fidelity against an expert panel benchmark (N=64 items) and conducted a pilot evaluation with 123 educators (70 primary teachers, 40 secondary teachers, 13 school leaders) recruited at an EIE conference. Gemini demonstrated high alignment with expert evaluations (97%), matching or exceeding static baseline feedback in user satisfaction (Mean = 4.1/5 vs. 3.8/5). Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 participant objections revealed key areas of tension, particularly around contextual constraints and pedagogical subjectivity. While the findings validate the technical proof-of-concept, system usability, and user engagement of ETQ-AI as an interactive scaffolding interface, we emphasize that this pilot study measures user perceptions and conversational patterns rather than direct pre/post shifts in critical reflection or classroom instructional practice.

title: Quality-by-Design Framework for Evaluating AI-Driven Machine Translation in Regulatory Affairs
abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine translation increasingly prepares multilingual product information for EU marketing authorisation, yet no established process exists to adapt or validate a system for the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC), whose sections differ in regulatory function, terminology, and clinical risk. This work develops such a process and a qualification procedure against the approved human translation. Methods: An EMA-derived ontology divides the SmPC into seven regulatory domains, each with a provisional ICH Q9 risk profile, following Quality-by-Design principles. A No Language Left Behind model was fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation on an eight-language-pair corpus and compared with the pre-trained model using BLEU, chrF, TER and COMET. Quality was validated by a five-layer, human-sign-off pipeline. Results: Fine-tuning improved every metric for every language pair. Quality varied more by domain than by language, hidden by corpus-level scores, and the domains rated highest-risk, under provisional ratings awaiting external calibration, were not the best translated. Checks on language-independent quantities were reliable everywhere; within adverse-reaction sections, the terminology check was the only partial-anchor instrument, and it showed meaningful gains only after a second language-model stage. Conclusions: The fine-tuned model and its validation pipeline, targeting automated checks where reliable and human review elsewhere, form a promising assistive step under qualified sign-off whose suitability for production-scale deployment requires further validation; assessment must be by regulatory domain, not the document as a whole.

title: How Do Different Components Affect Story Illustration? From Narrative Processing to Prompt Repair
abstract: Illustrated stories support children&rsquo;s learning. They also aid digital publishing and preserve regional narratives. However, manual illustration is costly and difficult to scale. Diffusion models offer an alternative. Yet, they often omit narrative details. They may also alter recurring characters across scenes. This work tries to find answers to three research questions concerning diffusion-based story visualization. First, we study how scene segmentation and part-of-speech filtering influence narrative alignment. Second, we evaluate IP-Adapter and consistent self-attention for cross-scene identity preservation and examine their trade-offs with scene diversity and narrative fidelity. Finally, we propose an attention-guided prompt-repair method that measures the grounding of required entities, attributes, relations, and character states and then iteratively revises prompts. Our experiments indicate that image conditioning improves character continuity but can restrict scene variation. The proposed framework converts diffusion attention from a post hoc explanation into an automatic signal for diagnosing and repairing story prompts.

title: Benchmarking Local Large Language Models for Structured Knowledge Extraction in Conversational Commerce
abstract: The integration of natural language understanding into conversational commerce requires robustly extracting structured intents from idiomatic text. While cloud-based models are highly capable, their latency, privacy risks, and operational costs necessitate efficient local alternatives. To address this, we empirically evaluate locally deployed, open-weights Large Language Models (LLMs) on parsing multi-intent shopping cart commands into deterministic JSON schemas. We benchmark multiple models across minimal, extended, and few-shot prompting paradigms, utilizing a dual-axis framework to simultaneously measure extraction quality (operation F1-score, exact match, schema validity) and hardware performance (latency, GPU power consumption). Our evaluation highlights a fundamental trade-off between schema compliance and computational overhead, demonstrating how advanced prompting techniques improve parsing accuracy while measurably impacting inference latency and power draw. Ultimately, this comprehensive profiling identifies optimal model configurations for resource-constrained environments: a well-chosen 3-8B parameter model (specifically Granite4 3B) paired with few-shot prompting recovers over 95% of the quality of the largest evaluated model at a coarse indicative estimate of 40&times; lower operational energy per command, establishing a practical baseline for deploying cost-effective LLMs as efficiency candidates in resource-constrained environments.

title: BAP-YOLO: A Pear Disease and Pest Detection Algorithm for Natural Orchard Environments
abstract: Pest and disease detection in natural pear orchard environments is often affected by branch and leaf occlusion, non-uniform illumination, and complex background textures. In addition, substantial variations exist in the morphology and scale of lesions and insect-damaged regions, while the weak texture features of early-stage lesions can be progressively attenuated during feature propagation. Therefore, effectively representing targets at different scales while preserving discriminative local details and suppressing irrelevant background information is crucial for improving pest and disease detection in pear orchards. To address these challenges, this study proposes BAP-YOLO, a detection framework designed for natural pear orchard environments. The framework progressively enhances feature representation through context aggregation, adaptive scale modeling, and discriminative detail refinement. First, a Branch-based Target Enhancement Fusion (BTEF) module is introduced into the backbone network to enhance hierarchical feature representations at multiple backbone stages, thereby reducing interference from complex background information in target representation. Second, an Adaptive Scale Dynamic (ASD) module is designed and embedded into the neck network to construct candidate features with different effective receptive fields and dynamically modulate their contributions using multi-resolution statistics, thereby improving the model&rsquo;s ability to detect targets with substantial scale variations. Finally, a Parallel Nonlinear Enhancement (PNE) module is incorporated between the neck network and detection head to enrich weak-texture and local-detail representations through complementary nonlinear transformations and element-wise fusion before prediction. Experiments were conducted on a pear orchard image dataset containing six classes: beetle, black_block, dry blight, health, rust, and scab. The experimental results showed that BAP-YOLO achieved a precision of 0.854, an mAP@50 of 0.876, and an F1-score of 0.826. Compared with the baseline YOLO11n, BAP-YOLO improved Precision, mAP@50, and F1-score by 6.1, 2.1, and 1.3 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of BAP-YOLO for pear disease and pest detection in natural orchard images.

title: Social Media Analytics for Evaluating Digital Marketing Performance: The Case of Olive Oil Enterprises in Greece
abstract: Social media (SM) platforms are widely used for corporate communication, yet quantitative evidence from specialized agri-food sectors remains limited. This study evaluates the SM adoption, activity, audience growth, interaction efficiency, and interaction concentration of the 511 Greek enterprises registered for Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) and/or Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) olive oil. Adoption was modeled at the enterprise level using logistic regression, and key performance indicators for 116 Facebook, 70 Instagram, and 32 YouTube profiles were compared between the first halves of 2025 and 2026 using paired, multiplicity-corrected tests. Only 28.2% of enterprises maintained at least one official profile; adoption was higher among standardization- and commercialization-oriented enterprises and among companies than among sole proprietors. Cooperatives had the lowest descriptive adoption rate (13.1%). Follower counts increased significantly on all three platforms, but median gains were small, whereas no posting or interaction indicator changed significantly. Inactivity was persistent, inactive Facebook pages tended to lose followers, and interactions were highly concentrated, even among active profiles. Posting volume was associated with audience growth and cumulative interactions but not with interactions per post, and an exploratory analysis of message features found no association that was consistent across both periods. For certified producers, the key decision is less whether to open a profile than whether it can be sustained, and follower counts alone are a misleading measure of performance.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Decision Support Systems: Contributions, Emerging Patterns, and Future Directions
abstract: Decision-making is one of the most fundamental activities in many human, organizational, scientific, and societal contexts [...]

title: Leakage-Controlled and Calibrated Deep Ensemble Learning for Reliable COVID-19 Classification from Chest X-Ray and CT Images
abstract: Reliable evaluation of artificial intelligence models for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) imaging remains challenging because patient-level dependencies, source-related biases, and differences between imaging modalities can lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, modality-aware deep ensemble framework for COVID-19 classification using chest X-ray (CXR) and computed tomography (CT) images from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and the SARS-CoV-2 CT-Scan Dataset. Separate evaluation protocols were established for CXR and CT, with duplicate control and available source information incorporated for CXR and patient-level partitioning applied to CT before data augmentation. Four ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs)&mdash;VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet169, and InceptionV3&mdash;were evaluated, followed by temperature scaling for probability calibration and validation-optimized weighted soft voting for ensemble fusion. The original CT architectural comparison was conducted at the slice level, whereas the final CT evaluation was performed at the patient level. In the final modality-specific held-out evaluation, DenseNet169 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.985, an accuracy of 97.32%, and an F1-score of 98.1% on the 2870-image CXR test set. The calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.990, an accuracy of 98.43%, and an F1-score of 97.9%, with a Brier score of 0.030 and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.023. For CT, DenseNet169 achieved an AUROC of 0.941 and correctly classified 16 of 18 patients (88.89%), whereas the calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.969 and correctly classified 17 of 18 patients (94.44%), with a Brier score of 0.070 and an ECE of 0.053. An uncertainty-aware selective-prediction analysis identified 316 of 2870 CXR test images (11.01%) and 2 of 18 CT test patients (11.11%) as low-confidence cases for specialist review. Among the remaining CT cases, 15 of 16 patients were correctly classified (93.75%). Because the CT test cohort contained only 18 patients, the patient-level CT performance and selective-prediction results should be interpreted cautiously as descriptive estimates from this limited cohort. The original pooled evaluation, in which DenseNet169 achieved 98.51% accuracy, is retained only as an exploratory architectural comparison and should not be interpreted as directly comparable with the final modality-specific evaluation. The findings demonstrate that evaluation design, statistical unit, probability calibration, and ensemble fusion materially influence the interpretation of COVID-19 imaging-classification performance. The proposed framework provides leakage-aware and calibrated performance estimates under the evaluated datasets; however, independent multicenter external validation is required before broader claims of clinical generalizability or deployment readiness can be made.

title: Dependency Restructuring: How Technological Enactment Changes Organizational Requirement Relations
abstract: Digital technologies can change organizational work without changing the dependencies through which work is coordinated. This article examines the cases in which those dependencies do change. The analysis separates changes in activities from changes in dependencies and from the coordination needed to manage them. Its main contribution is a bounded meso-level framework that treats dependency restructuring as an independently observable change between technological enactment and subsequent coordination requirements. The framework specifies observable forms of dependency change and derives two conditional propositions. Individual dependency relations may be created, eliminated, or redirected to a different provider; previously separate sets of dependencies may also become connected. The first proposition concerns situations in which local autonomy increases while reliance on a shared technological or external capability also increases. The second concerns situations in which different technologies produce similar coordination requirements because they generate similar dependency configurations under similar organizational conditions. Two evidence-based illustrations&mdash;enterprise cloud migration and artificial intelligence integration in organizational workflows&mdash;show how the approach can be applied without treating the cases as tests of the theory. The article also provides an empirical identification procedure for distinguishing activity change, dependency change, and coordination response.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Kazakh-Language Educational Assistants: Sentiment Classification and Question Answering with and Without Context
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in education, but evidence on their performance comes mainly from high-resource languages. We evaluated five commercial LLMs in Kazakh in a zero-shot setting: sentiment classification on 300 class-balanced KazSAnDRA reviews and question answering (QA) on the same 300 randomly sampled KazQAD questions with and without the gold supporting passage. Exact McNemar tests with Holm correction found no significant pairwise differences on sentiment classification, one with supporting context, and nine without context under the Containment criterion. For OpenAI and Anthropic, the higher-tier model had a larger advantage over its lower-tier counterpart when the supporting passage was removed (tier-by-regime interaction: OR = 1.92, 95% CI [1.52, 2.43]). Closed-book scores were affected by output format, inflectional morphology, and answer length. Human evaluation of 500 QA responses showed that string-based metrics substantially underestimated closed-book accuracy (0.55 by human judgement versus 0.26 by Containment). Under human judgement, the three higher-scoring models did not differ significantly from one another. Access to a relevant passage narrowed differences between models, although this oracle-context condition did not test a retrieval system. These findings support task-specific evaluation of Kazakh-language educational assistants and the use of answer-matching criteria checked against human judgement.

title: A Survey of Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Based on Tree Representation
abstract: Smart contracts, characterized by automation, transparency, and decentralization, can establish efficient, secure, and reliable blockchain fund management and data processing mechanisms, playing a crucial supporting role in blockchain application scenarios. However, security issues in smart contracts are increasingly prominent, making vulnerability detection a critical research focus; detection methods based on tree representation have emerged as a promising direction in this field. A comprehensive review of tree representation-based smart contract vulnerability detection methods is provided in this paper, aiming to offer new insights and theoretical support for smart contract security. First, a three-level vulnerability taxonomy covering 18 common smart contract vulnerability types is presented, categorized by the specific stage of the smart contract life cycle where the vulnerability originates: the Solidity code layer, the EVM execution layer, and the blockchain system layer. Second, four traditional detection paradigms&mdash;formal verification, symbolic execution, fuzz testing, and static analysis&mdash;are characterized by their core mechanisms and compared across multiple performance dimensions. Third, following the PRISMA systematic review guidelines, 23 primary studies on tree representation-based methods are selected and organized under a novel three-category taxonomy: pure AST sequentialization/traversal, tree-structured neural networks, and AST-to-graph transformations. The technical and application-level challenges of these methods are synthesized, and corresponding open research questions and improvement directions are discussed to inform future work.

title: Measuring Versioned Information Releases and Observable Complementor Links in Generative AI Platform Ecosystems
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) model repositories expose versioned information artifacts, but public platform records rarely provide complete adoption histories. This study develops a reproducible architecture for measuring temporal relations between repository documentation (README) revision candidates and observable public complementor links. A task-stratified frame of 3577 models, fixed before downstream outcomes were measured, yielded 365 eligible candidates and 311 matched pairs. Exact model identifiers in public Spaces were traced to repository versions, producing 8137 current model&ndash;Space relations and 5316 locatable first appearances. A separately frozen Wave 3 frame of 1440 unused models yielded 62 candidates and 43 pre-event-balanced pairs. This study reports fixed-rule event families, documented matching conditions, full-coverage public link tracing, a linear difference-in-differences specification, and paired-label randomization. Across the primary, enhanced, independent, and pooled designs, confidence intervals include zero and the paired tests do not support stable average differences across pairs. The contribution is an auditable architecture that separates event construction, relationship observability, comparison design, cohort replication, and inference. It does not validate a semantic actionability classifier, measure total adoption, or estimate a causal documentation effect.

title: Understanding Student Adoption of Gamified Learning Tools in Jordanian Higher Education: Integrating the Big Five Personality Traits and the Technology Acceptance Model
abstract: This study examined the relationships involving the Big Five personality traits, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, behavioral intention, and continued usage intention in gamified learning technologies in Jordanian higher education. This study integrated the Big Five personality framework with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to investigate how individual personality characteristics are associated with students&rsquo; perceptions toward adopting gamified learning technologies. Data were collected from 600 university students using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings revealed that both perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use significantly influenced students&rsquo; behavioral intention, while behavioral intention significantly predicted continued usage intention. Contrary to the original TAM, perceived ease of use did not significantly influence perceived usefulness. Results further indicated that the effects of personality traits were mixed. Specifically, agreeableness demonstrated significant positive relationships with both perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, whereas openness to experience and extraversion significantly influenced perceived usefulness only. In contrast, conscientiousness did not significantly influence either perceived usefulness or perceived ease of use, while neuroticism significantly influenced perceived ease of use but not perceived usefulness. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of considering both personality characteristics and technology acceptance factors when examining students&rsquo; perceptions toward adopting gamified learning technologies in higher education. As this study employed a cross-sectional research design, the reported relationships should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than evidence of causality.

title: Factors Affecting the Use of Digital Banking: A Literature Review
abstract: In recent years, digital technology has brought major changes to financial services. These rapid changes have created both new opportunities and challenges for digital banking. This has encouraged researchers to study and investigate this phenomenon. Thus, this narrative review includes 35 peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2026. It explores what motivates people from different countries and backgrounds to start using digital banking. The main factors are organised using several frameworks: Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), Task-Technology Fit (TTF), and Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE). These frameworks combine the key factors into six areas: trust and security; perceived usefulness and ease of use; customer experience and service quality; technological infrastructure and compatibility; demographic and socioeconomic factors; and institutional and regulatory influences. Thus, people are more likely to use digital banking if they trust it, find it easy to use, and believe it is safe. Age, education, and digital skills also affect adoption. Although digital banking is becoming more common, it still faces challenges such as privacy concerns, complex technology, limited digital infrastructure, and unclear regulations. This review highlights the main reasons people use financial technology and offers suggestions to make digital banking easier and more accessible.

title: From Static Preservation to Dynamic Continuity: The Historical Evolution of Architectural Heritage Restoration Methods
abstract: Architectural heritage restoration has expanded rapidly, yet its knowledge base remains fragmented across materials, structural assessment, digital technologies, and conservation management. This study maps the field&rsquo;s historical evolution and intellectual structure through a bibliometric review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA), comprising 248 English-language articles and reviews indexed in Web of Science from 1997 to April 2026. VOSviewer version 1.6.20, CiteSpace version 6.4.R1, and Bibliometrix version 5.4.1 were used to analyse publication trends, co-occurrence networks, citation structures, and thematic evolution. Four findings emerge: (1) restoration has shifted from localized, experience-based repair toward evidence-based, integrated conservation; (2) research has progressed from strength-oriented intervention to material compatibility, authenticity, and continued use; (3) digital technologies are evolving from static documentation toward knowledge integration, predictive diagnosis, and life-cycle management; and (4) preventive conservation increasingly links cultural value, environmental exposure, resilience, and multi-hazard risk. Five interdependent domains&mdash;material restoration, digital modelling, non-destructive testing, restoration resilience, and preventive conservation&mdash;structure the field. The study proposes an iterative framework integrating value assessment, material&ndash;structural evidence, digital information, risk prevention, and long-term maintenance to support dynamic continuity in architectural heritage conservation.

title: Calibrating Large Language Models for Educational Assessment: A Reliability-Weighted Contextual Calibration Framework for CTT Item Facility and Discrimination Estimation
abstract: Item facility and item discrimination are two frequently used indices in Classical Test Theory (CTT) for evaluating examination quality. This study evaluates four state-of-the-art LLMs&mdash;ChatGPT, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao&mdash;by comparing their predicted item facility and discrimination with empirical CTT estimates computed from undergraduate mathematics examinations. To improve the consistency of LLM-generated estimates, we propose a Reliability-Weighted Contextual Calibration Framework (RCCF), which combines reliability-weighted model aggregation with contextual information from historical assessments. The framework is evaluated using a nested leave-one-item-out cross-validation (LOOCV) procedure. Experimental results show that RCCF demonstrates competitive performance across the evaluated assessment settings and CTT parameters, while its relative advantage over individual LLMs and ablation models varies across tasks. By integrating multiple LLM estimates with available historical and contextual assessment information, RCCF provides a practical framework for preliminary CTT parameter estimation, with further prospective validation needed to establish its generalizability to unseen examinations.

title: Weekly Cyber-Threat Seasonality Varies with National Weekend Convention: A Cross-National Forecasting Benchmark
abstract: Weekly cycles in cyber-threat activity are well documented, but how their timing varies with national weekends is not. Across 384 series from 192 countries, the weekly cycle is nearly universal. In the 43 countries whose weekend we individually sourced, its phase is statistically associated with the local working week. Under the dataset&rsquo;s date labels, activity is lowest on each country&rsquo;s own first working day (Sunday) in every Friday&ndash;Saturday-weekend country. In just over half of Saturday&ndash;Sunday countries, it is lowest one day later (Tuesday rather than Monday). This separation survives any uniform shift of the labels; the absolute weekday depends on an undocumented source timezone. Amplitude is larger under Friday&ndash;Saturday weekends (p = 0.0010). Auditing the benchmark, we also found that its ambiguous date format, read with a common parsing idiom, silently discards 59.9% of the data. A full factorial of day-of-week specification, multi-step strategy, and learner, with reimplemented baselines, rolling-origin evaluation, and Diebold&ndash;Mariano/Holm inference, shows that specification improves every stable pairing at H = 10 (factors 0.57&ndash;0.87) and wins on 190 of 192 countries. It is not sufficient: the multilayer perceptron still loses to a seven-observation moving average. No learned model significantly beats a fixed-window seasonal decomposition at either operational horizon. Accuracy here is governed by specification, not architecture.

title: Real-Time Markerless Motion Capture for Interactive Applications and Game Engines: Pipelines, Spatio-Temporal Refinement, and Latency Budgets
abstract: The rapid evolution of deep learning and computer vision has transformed markerless motion capture (MoCap) from specialized biomechanical tools into a key technology for real-time interactive systems, video game engines, and virtual production. This review analyzes state-of-the-art markerless pipelines and focuses on integrating 3D human pose estimation (HPE) into standard graphics engines. We evaluate the shift from single-view regression to temporal convolutional architectures. Our review emphasizes the trade-offs between spatial precision and algorithmic overhead for interactive use cases. Central to our analysis is the spatio-temporal refinement of noisy skeletal data. We assess adaptive smoothing techniques, such as the 1-Euro filter and predictive neural filtering, designed to minimize jitter and motion-to-photon latency. Findings indicate that modern markerless systems approach the standards of marker-based tools. However, maintaining temporal consistency under strict real-time budgets remains a fundamental challenge for human-display feedback loops. We examine industry-standard engines and their role in permitting seamless character retargeting throughout diverse applications, including clinical monitoring and sports coaching. Ultimately, this work synthesizes methodologies to optimize the responsiveness of AI-based MoCap systems within contemporary real-time software architectures.

title: Appropriate Reliance on AI Decision Support Systems: A Sociotechnical Narrative Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly supports human decision making, but effective use depends on whether users assign AI advice the decision weight it warrants. This theory-oriented narrative review synthesizes 29 core studies, together with recent reviews and foundational theory, to examine appropriate reliance, overreliance, and underreliance in AI-supported decisions. The synthesis identifies five recurring sociotechnical conditions shaping reliance: system, user, task, interaction, and organization. Findings show that explanations, uncertainty cues, expertise, self-confidence, prior experience, and organizational incentives affect reliance differently across settings, while trust and reliance evolve through feedback over time. Interventions that reduce overreliance may also increase underreliance. The resulting framework centers warranted behavioral decision weight, comparative evaluation of AI and self-capability, and temporal feedback, shifting attention from increasing trust or AI use toward supporting context-sensitive allocation of decision weight.

title: Distributed Authorization and Reliability-Aware Hardware Security for Photovoltaic Monitoring
abstract: Unattended photovoltaic monitoring nodes must maintain authenticated operation under physical access, intermittent connectivity, and environmentally induced key-reconstruction errors. We present a distributed adaptive hardware security framework (DAHSF) combining trusted-gateway threshold authorization, adaptive static random-access memory (SRAM) physical unclonable function (PUF) reconstruction, and incident-driven inspection. Independent epoch secrets separate current authorization from retained historical shares. A nested Bose&ndash;Chaudhuri&ndash;Hocquenghem (BCH) error-correction scheme reconstructs a fixed 2016-bit SRAM-PUF response, from which universal hashing extracts a 256-bit seed; federated estimation guides decoding effort. The cost and defense trade-offs are assessed under the tested workload, gateway trust, prediction-calibration, and availability conditions. On a 30-node ESP32 platform, DAHSF reduces median startup and mean node power by 4.8% and 4.4% relative to a matched lightweight baseline, with 14.3% more incremental RAM. Predicted-bound decoding reduces mean decoding time from 96 to 59 microseconds. A separate confirmatory cohort records three failures in 120,000 stressed reconstructions; its board-clustered 95% upper bound is 8.6&times;10&minus;5. In the moderate attack scenario, the full inspection profile reduces compromised-node exposure by 30.0% relative to a risk-threshold policy and by 18.0% relative to frozen propagation-rate estimates. The recorded control workload has no observed 1 ms MPPT deadline misses, while fault injection still bypasses authorization in 168 of 4000 attempts.

title: Calibrated Prediction of Students&rsquo; Next Responses in Digital Mathematics Learning: A Completion-Ordered and Cold-Start-Aware Framework
abstract: Digital mathematics platforms support probabilistic prediction of subsequent student responses, but temporal ordering, score comparability and calibration affect the validity of evaluation. We evaluated AdaptiveMath-AI on a deterministic cohort of 385,037 Eedi interactions from 2904 students. Early representations were frozen before supervised fitting; learner states were reconstructed in recorded completion order, with simultaneous events predicted before batch updates. Twenty-two numerical inputs supported a gradient-boosting anchor, regularized item corrections, valid curriculum fallback and separately selected calibration. Six monthly expanding-window evaluations, repeated across ten seeds, covered 143,565 responses. The primary estimand averaged within-month performance differences rather than ranking scores from different fitted windows together. Mean monthly ROC-AUC was 0.761173 for AdaptiveMath-AI and 0.756833 for the 100-iteration comparator; the paired difference was 0.004339 (95% conditional student-cluster interval, 0.003636&ndash;0.005131). Mean monthly log loss and Brier score were 0.544721 and 0.184383. Independently calibrated ablations supported the contribution of question correction but not an additional hierarchy benefit. Against a recency-matched question-rate control, question-only residual correction improved ROC-AUC by 0.000628 (0.000304&ndash;0.000928). Calibration superiority was not uniform. The contribution is a temporally explicit, reproducible evaluation of item adaptation, not a new foundational architecture. Missing presentation timestamps and the previously studied single-platform source limit prospective, external and educational-utility claims.

title: QSNA: Base-Conditioned Low-Rank Residual Refinement for Retention-Constrained Open-Vocabulary Detection on ROADWork
abstract: Adapting an open-vocabulary detector to work-zone imagery can improve target recognition but may reduce performance on source-domain and large-vocabulary benchmarks, represented here by COCO and LVIS. Replay and model merging can produce retention-aware checkpoints, but they do not by themselves provide a dedicated local refinement step after checkpoint selection. We propose Query Spectral-Null Adapter (QSNA), a complementary local update applied after checkpoint selection. QSNA freezes the selected checkpoint and learns an 8064-parameter low-rank residual at a single decoder FFN output projection, constrained by an estimated source-gradient complement. The residual can be rescaled after training and folded directly into the checkpoint. On the primary replay-derived checkpoint, QSNA raised ROADWork AP from 28.18 to 28.30, a +0.12 AP change, while COCO and LVIS AP decreased by 0.09 and 0.16 relative to the base. Across three fixed-base adapter seeds, the primary configuration produced similar descriptive ROADWork changes of about +0.13 AP and all three seeds remained above the adopted retention floors; this is replication evidence, not a significance test. Across nine base-specific fits, ROADWork AP repeatedly rose over a finite residual-scale range and then turned over, with the feasible range governed by the starting checkpoint. Canonical random, unconstrained, and projection-removed controls show that update orientation changes the acquisition&ndash;retention response, but they do not establish spectral projection as necessary or universally superior. Together, these results position QSNA as a base-conditioned, deployment-oriented local refinement stage after retention-aware checkpoint construction.

title: Comparing LoRA, DoRA, and OFT for Extremely Low-Resource English&ndash;Sango Machine Translation: Adaptation Performance and Out-of-Domain Retention
abstract: Extremely low-resource machine translation poses a difficult cross-lingual adaptation problem: improving target-language performance while preserving capabilities acquired through multilingual pretraining. This study compares three mathematically distinct parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods&mdash;LoRA, DoRA, and orthogonal fine-tuning (OFT)&mdash;for English&ndash;Sango translation using NLLB-200-distilled-600M, a deterministically constructed 9000-pair corpus, and three random seeds per method. Following standard domain-adaptation practice, adaptation-test performance and out-of-domain (OOD) change were evaluated separately using a native-speaker-validated adaptation test set and FLORES+ devtest, with corpus chrF as the primary metric and paired bootstrap testing with Holm correction. All nine adapted runs scored below zero-shot NLLB-200 on the complete adaptation test and FLORES+ devtest. However, the adaptation-side estimate was composition-sensitive: the descriptive direction reversed on the 38-item A-only subset, and checkpoint selection used an all-A development set whereas the final test was B-dominated. The complete adaptation-test result is therefore treated as exploratory. By contrast, the negative FLORES+ pattern was consistent across all nine adapted runs and persisted at fixed final checkpoints, making out-of-domain degradation the most stable performance finding. The methods nevertheless differed computationally: OFT used approximately one quarter of the trainable parameters required by LoRA or DoRA, whereas LoRA achieved the shortest wall-clock training time. These results provide a controlled multi-seed comparison of structurally distinct PEFT configurations for an extremely low-resource English&ndash;Sango setting and highlight the importance of considering data quality, zero-shot baselines, training variability, and computational efficiency alongside translation performance.

title: Fuzzy-Enhanced Transformer&ndash;CNN Feature Fusion for Robust Steel Alloy Classification Using Femtosecond Laser-Ablation Spark-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy
abstract: Accurate steel alloy classification is a core task in industrial quality control, yet laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) data suffers from spectral noise, matrix effects, and multi-element peak overlap. Femtosecond laser-ablation spark-induced breakdown spectroscopy (fs-LA-SIBS) enables high-sensitivity detection, but plasma fluctuations degrade the performance of conventional chemometric methods and standalone deep learning models. To address these issues, we propose HybridTFNet, a hybrid fuzzy-Transformer-convolutional neural network (CNN) framework for uncertainty-aware spectral learning and multi-scale feature fusion. A fuzzy logic layer with Gaussian membership functions quantifies spectral uncertainty and suppresses noise-dominated regions. A Transformer encoder captures long-range wavelength dependencies and global inter-element coupling, while a one-dimensional CNN extracts fine-grained local features such as characteristic peaks and wavelength shifts. Adaptive fusion of global and local representations constructs a highly discriminative feature space for classification. Experiments on nine certified steel alloy fs-LA-SIBS datasets show that HybridTFNet achieves 100% classification accuracy across four independent test sets, significantly outperforming traditional machine learning (PLS, KNN, RF) and deep learning models (CNN, LSTM, Transformer). Multi-test-set evaluation on the current dataset indicates stable classification performance; we note that all results are from a single representative run, and variability across repeated runs is not quantified in this work. With low complexity and low inference latency, the proposed framework is suitable for near-real-time industrial deployment, providing an effective solution for intelligent spectral information processing.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Integration of Satellite, Cellular, and Wi-Fi Networks for Reliable and Resilient Smart City Connectivity: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The rapid development of smart cities requires reliable and resilient connectivity across heterogeneous communication environments, while no single access technology can simultaneously satisfy requirements for coverage, mobility, latency, capacity, and service continuity. This review investigates the integration of satellite, cellular, and Wi-Fi networks and examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enabling coordinated multi-access connectivity. A PRISMA-guided systematic literature search and study-selection procedure was applied to peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2026, resulting in 36 peer-reviewed publications included in the qualitative synthesis. The selected studies were analyzed across eight thematic areas, including satellite&ndash;terrestrial integration, cellular&ndash;Wi-Fi convergence, vertical handover, AI/DRL-based mobility management, integrated terrestrial&ndash;non-terrestrial networks, resilience, smart city communication infrastructure, and multi-connectivity. The analysis shows that satellite&ndash;cellular integration, terrestrial Multi-RAT coordination, AI-based handover, and multi-connectivity have been extensively investigated as individual research directions; however, their convergence within a unified satellite&ndash;cellular&ndash;Wi-Fi framework remains limited. Existing solutions are also predominantly reactive and rarely combine predictive network management, service-aware decision-making, and resilience objectives. The review therefore identifies predictive AI-driven multi-access orchestration integrating satellite, cellular, and Wi-Fi connectivity as a promising direction for resilient smart city communication infrastructures.

title: Cross-Case Applicability and Comparability of an Information Environment Vulnerability Assessment Methodology: A Comparative Case Study
abstract: This study examines the cross-case applicability and comparability of an information environment vulnerability assessment methodology in two functionally different university workplaces: a university library and a university institute. The study uses a comparative multi-case design to assess information providers and users through three complementary procedures: a context-specific semi-quantitative assessment, a common binary conformity assessment, and a weighted thematic analysis. Under the common descriptive classification framework, the overall outputs of all three procedures fall within the medium interval. The university institute has higher overall numerical values in each procedure, although the degree of direct comparability varies among them. At the perspective-specific level, the provider result for the university institute in Method 1 is 60.0% and falls within the high interval. Provider-side numerical outputs exceed user-side outputs in both workplaces. The comparison also shows that similar aggregate values can arise from different vulnerability structures, with the workplaces differing in the distribution of process, communication, documentation, technological, and information-interpretation vulnerabilities. The findings support procedural applicability and comparative interpretability across the two examined workplaces under a single-evaluator design. Broader transferability across independent organisations and assessors, however, remains to be established, and the assessment instrument requires further validation.

title: Evaluating Semantic Artifact Continuity for Noisy Social Text: RDF Materialization, SHACL Conformance, and Model Input Evidence
abstract: Noisy social text can be transformed into semantic representations, but evaluating the resulting artifacts is difficult when source records, ontology activations, graph resources, conformance reports, and model inputs are considered separately. The evaluation problem is whether their connections remain inspectable as these artifacts are generated and used. This study examines the above continuity using 1614 Reddit posts about artificial intelligence and technology. Ontology activations produce sibling Resource Description Framework (RDF) and numeric representations linked through stable identifiers. Explicit correspondence checks and controlled fault tests examine these connections, while Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) checks assess conformance to declared graph constraints. Existing verification checks detect 15 of 22 injected continuity faults. The remaining seven are detected only by supplementary diagnostics. Separate human assessment of 120 validation texts evaluates concept presence and local polarity against the source text, distinguishing extraction quality from artifact continuity. Downstream classification provides secondary evidence of modest mean macro-F1 gains in agreement with inherited lexical labels, varying by model across three seeds on one fixed split. The contribution is an evaluation of governed semantic artifact continuity at the post and variable levels, making the connections among these artifacts and their failure conditions clear and inspectable.
